import tkinter as tk
import ttkbootstrap as ttk
from ttkbootstrap.constants import *

class AnalysisTab(ttk.Frame):
    def __init__(self, master, app):
        super().__init__(master)
        self.app = app
        self._build_ui()

    def _build_ui(self):
        # Main container with padding - Using ScrolledFrame to be safe on small screens
        # but configured to fill space
        
        # Note: ttkbootstrap has a ScrolledFrame, but let's stick to standard grid layout 
        # inside the tab for better control, assuming the window size is large enough (1200x900 default)
        
        main_container = ttk.Frame(self, padding=20)
        main_container.pack(fill=BOTH, expand=True)
        
        # Grid Configuration
        main_container.columnconfigure(0, weight=1, uniform="group1") # Left Col
        main_container.columnconfigure(1, weight=1, uniform="group1") # Right Col
        main_container.rowconfigure(0, weight=1) # Main content area
        
        # Left Column Container
        left_col = ttk.Frame(main_container)
        left_col.grid(row=0, column=0, sticky="nsew", padx=(0, 15))
        
        # Right Column Container
        right_col = ttk.Frame(main_container)
        right_col.grid(row=0, column=1, sticky="nsew", padx=(15, 0))
        
        # --- LEFT COLUMN ---
        
        # 1. Project & Input
        p_frame = ttk.Labelframe(left_col, text="Project & Input", padding=15, bootstyle="info")
        p_frame.pack(fill=X, pady=(0, 20))
        
        ttk.Label(p_frame, text="Project Name:").pack(anchor="w")
        ttk.Combobox(p_frame, textvariable=self.app.project_var, values=self.app.available_projects).pack(fill=X, pady=(5, 10))
        
        ttk.Button(p_frame, text="Select Image", command=self.app.select_image, bootstyle="secondary-outline").pack(fill=X, pady=(5, 5))
        ttk.Label(p_frame, textvariable=self.app.image_path_var, wraplength=400, font=("TkDefaultFont", 8)).pack(anchor="w", pady=5)

        # 2. Metadata Overrides
        m_frame = ttk.Labelframe(left_col, text="Metadata Overrides", padding=15, bootstyle="info")
        m_frame.pack(fill=X, pady=(0, 20))
        
        # Use grid inside for aligned labels/entries
        m_frame.columnconfigure(1, weight=1)
        
        ttk.Label(m_frame, text="Part Number:").grid(row=0, column=0, sticky="w", pady=5)
        ttk.Entry(m_frame, textvariable=self.app.part_number_var).grid(row=0, column=1, sticky="ew", padx=5, pady=5)
        
        ttk.Label(m_frame, text="Thickness:").grid(row=1, column=0, sticky="w", pady=5)
        ttk.Entry(m_frame, textvariable=self.app.thickness_var).grid(row=1, column=1, sticky="ew", padx=5, pady=5)
        
        ttk.Label(m_frame, text="Author:").grid(row=2, column=0, sticky="w", pady=5)
        ttk.Entry(m_frame, textvariable=self.app.author_var).grid(row=2, column=1, sticky="ew", padx=5, pady=5)

        # 3. Color Correction
        cc_frame = ttk.Labelframe(left_col, text="Color Correction", padding=15, bootstyle="info")
        cc_frame.pack(fill=X)
        
        ttk.Checkbutton(cc_frame, text="Enable Color Alignment", variable=self.app.color_alignment_var, bootstyle="round-toggle").pack(anchor="w", pady=5)
        
        self.cc_sub_frame = ttk.Frame(cc_frame)
        self.cc_sub_frame.pack(fill=X, pady=5)
        ttk.Label(self.cc_sub_frame, text="Method:").pack(side=LEFT)
        ttk.Combobox(self.cc_sub_frame, textvariable=self.app.color_correction_method_var, values=["linear", "polynomial", "hsv", "histogram"]).pack(side=LEFT, fill=X, expand=True, padx=5)
        
        self.cc_btn_checker = ttk.Button(cc_frame, text="Select Sample Checker (Optional)", command=self.app.select_color_checker, bootstyle="secondary-outline")

        ttk.Label(cc_frame, textvariable=self.app.color_checker_path_var, wraplength=400, font=("TkDefaultFont", 8)).pack(anchor="w")

        def update_cc_state(*args):
            state = NORMAL if self.app.color_alignment_var.get() else DISABLED
            for child in self.cc_sub_frame.winfo_children():
                child.configure(state=state)
            self.cc_btn_checker.configure(state=state)
        
        self.app.color_alignment_var.trace_add("write", update_cc_state)
        update_cc_state()

        # --- RIGHT COLUMN ---
        
        # 4. Alignment & Masking
        if self.app.debug_mode:
            am_frame = ttk.Labelframe(right_col, text="Alignment & Masking", padding=15, bootstyle="warning")
            am_frame.pack(fill=X, pady=(0, 20))
            
            ttk.Checkbutton(am_frame, text="ArUco Alignment", variable=self.app.alignment_var, bootstyle="square-toggle").pack(anchor="w", pady=2)
            ttk.Checkbutton(am_frame, text="Object Alignment", variable=self.app.object_alignment_var, bootstyle="square-toggle").pack(anchor="w", pady=2)
            
            shad_frame = ttk.Frame(am_frame)
            shad_frame.pack(fill=X, pady=5)
            ttk.Label(shad_frame, text="Shadow Removal:").pack(side=LEFT)
            ttk.Combobox(shad_frame, textvariable=self.app.object_alignment_shadow_removal_var, values=["clahe", "gamma", "none"]).pack(side=LEFT, fill=X, expand=True, padx=5)
            
            ttk.Separator(am_frame, orient=HORIZONTAL).pack(fill=X, pady=10)
            
            ttk.Checkbutton(am_frame, text="Apply Drawing Mask", variable=self.app.apply_mask_var, bootstyle="square-toggle").pack(anchor="w", pady=2)
            
            self.mask_info_lbl = ttk.Label(am_frame, text="(Using Project-defined Layers)", font=("Helvetica", 8), foreground="gray")
            self.mask_info_lbl.pack(anchor="w", padx=25)

            def update_mask_state(*args):
                state = NORMAL if self.app.apply_mask_var.get() else DISABLED
                self.mask_info_lbl.configure(state=state)
            
            self.app.apply_mask_var.trace_add("write", update_mask_state)
            update_mask_state()

        # 5. Analysis & Processing
        if self.app.debug_mode:
            an_frame = ttk.Labelframe(right_col, text="Analysis & Processing", padding=15, bootstyle="success")
            an_frame.pack(fill=X)
            
            ttk.Checkbutton(an_frame, text="Gaussian Blur", variable=self.app.blur_var, bootstyle="round-toggle").pack(anchor="w", pady=2)
            
            ttk.Checkbutton(an_frame, text="Aggregate Matched Pixels", variable=self.app.aggregate_var, bootstyle="round-toggle").pack(anchor="w", pady=2)
            
            self.agg_sub_frame = ttk.Frame(an_frame)
            self.agg_sub_frame.pack(fill=X, pady=5)
            
            # Small grid for agg params
            self.agg_sub_frame.columnconfigure((1,3,5), weight=1)
            ttk.Label(self.agg_sub_frame, text="Kernel:").grid(row=0, column=0, padx=(0,5))
            ttk.Entry(self.agg_sub_frame, textvariable=self.app.agg_kernel_size_var, width=5).grid(row=0, column=1, sticky="ew")
            
            ttk.Label(self.agg_sub_frame, text="Min Area:").grid(row=0, column=2, padx=(10,5))
            ttk.Entry(self.agg_sub_frame, textvariable=self.app.agg_min_area_var, width=8).grid(row=0, column=3, sticky="ew")
            
            ttk.Label(self.agg_sub_frame, text="Density:").grid(row=0, column=4, padx=(10,5))
            ttk.Entry(self.agg_sub_frame, textvariable=self.app.agg_density_thresh_var, width=5).grid(row=0, column=5, sticky="ew")

            def update_agg_state(*args):
                state = NORMAL if self.app.aggregate_var.get() else DISABLED
                for child in self.agg_sub_frame.winfo_children():
                    child.configure(state=state)
            
            self.app.aggregate_var.trace_add("write", update_agg_state)
            update_agg_state()
            
            ttk.Checkbutton(an_frame, text="Symmetry Analysis", variable=self.app.symmetry_var, bootstyle="round-toggle").pack(anchor="w", pady=(10, 5))
            
            # Sub-frame for specific symmetry types
            sym_sub = ttk.Frame(an_frame, padding=(20, 0, 0, 0))
            sym_sub.pack(fill=X)
            
            # Create a 2-column grid for symmetry checkboxes
            for i, (sym_type, var) in enumerate(self.app.symmetry_types_vars.items()):
                display_name = sym_type.replace('_', ' ').title()
                cb = ttk.Checkbutton(sym_sub, text=display_name, variable=var, bootstyle="secondary")
                cb.grid(row=i // 2, column=i % 2, sticky="w", pady=1)
                
                # Bind the state of these checkboxes to the main symmetry_var
                def update_state(st=sym_sub, sv=self.app.symmetry_var):
                    for child in st.winfo_children():
                        child.configure(state=NORMAL if sv.get() else DISABLED)
                
                # Initial state
                update_state()
                # Trace changes to symmetry_var
                self.app.symmetry_var.trace_add("write", lambda *args: update_state())

        # --- BOTTOM AREA (Buttons) ---
        bot_frame = ttk.Frame(main_container)
        bot_frame.grid(row=1, column=0, columnspan=2, sticky="ew", pady=(20, 0))
        
        # Make buttons taller
        ttk.Style().configure("Tall.TButton", font=("Helvetica", 12, "bold"))
        
        self.btn_start = ttk.Button(bot_frame, text="START FULL ANALYSIS", command=self._start_analysis_wrapper, 
                   bootstyle="success", style="Tall.TButton", width=20)
        self.btn_start.pack(fill=X, ipady=10, pady=(0, 10))
                   
        self.generate_pdf_button = ttk.Button(bot_frame, text="Generate PDF Report", command=self.app.generate_current_pdf,
                                            bootstyle="primary", style="Tall.TButton", state=DISABLED, width=20)
        self.generate_pdf_button.pack(fill=X, ipady=10)

    def _start_analysis_wrapper(self):
        """Disables the PDF button and starts analysis."""
        self.disable_pdf_button()
        self.app.run_analysis()

    def enable_pdf_button(self):
        self.generate_pdf_button.config(state=NORMAL)

    def disable_pdf_button(self):
        self.generate_pdf_button.config(state=DISABLED)

import tkinter as tk
import ttkbootstrap as ttk
from ttkbootstrap.constants import *
from tkinter import filedialog, messagebox
import os
import argparse
from src.pipeline import run_analysis
from src.utils.logging_utils import setup_logger

logger = setup_logger(__name__)

class BatchAnalysisTab(ttk.Frame):
    def __init__(self, master, app):
        super().__init__(master)
        self.app = app
        self.queue = [] # List of dictionaries
        self._build_ui()

    def _build_ui(self):
        # Layout: Left (Controls/Input), Right (Queue List)
        self.columnconfigure(0, weight=1) # Controls
        self.columnconfigure(1, weight=3) # List
        self.rowconfigure(0, weight=1)

        # --- Left Panel: Input Controls ---
        control_panel = ttk.Frame(self, padding=10)
        control_panel.grid(row=0, column=0, sticky="nsew")

        ttk.Label(control_panel, text="Batch Setup", font=("Helvetica", 12, "bold")).pack(anchor="w", pady=(0, 20))

        # Project Selection
        ttk.Label(control_panel, text="Project:").pack(anchor="w")
        self.cb_project = ttk.Combobox(control_panel, values=self.app.available_projects, state="readonly")
        self.cb_project.pack(fill=X, pady=(0, 10))

        # Image Selection
        ttk.Button(control_panel, text="Select Images...", command=self._select_images, bootstyle="primary-outline").pack(fill=X, pady=(0, 5))
        self.lbl_images = ttk.Label(control_panel, text="0 images selected", font=("Helvetica", 8))
        self.lbl_images.pack(anchor="w", pady=(0, 10))

        # Color Checker Selection
        ttk.Button(control_panel, text="Select Color Checker...", command=self._select_checker, bootstyle="secondary-outline").pack(fill=X, pady=(0, 5))
        self.checker_path = tk.StringVar()
        ttk.Label(control_panel, textvariable=self.checker_path, font=("Helvetica", 8), wraplength=200).pack(anchor="w", pady=(0, 20))

        # Add to Queue Button
        ttk.Button(control_panel, text="Add to Queue >>", command=self._add_to_queue, bootstyle="success").pack(fill=X, pady=(0, 20))
        
        ttk.Separator(control_panel, orient=HORIZONTAL).pack(fill=X, pady=10)

        # Run Button
        self.btn_run = ttk.Button(control_panel, text="RUN BATCH", command=self._run_batch, bootstyle="danger", width=15)
        self.btn_run.pack(fill=X, ipady=10)

        # --- Right Panel: Queue List ---
        list_panel = ttk.Frame(self, padding=10)
        list_panel.grid(row=0, column=1, sticky="nsew")
        
        ttk.Label(list_panel, text="Processing Queue", font=("Helvetica", 12, "bold")).pack(anchor="w", pady=(0, 10))

        # Treeview
        columns = ("project", "image", "checker")
        self.tree = ttk.Treeview(list_panel, columns=columns, show="headings", bootstyle="info")
        self.tree.heading("project", text="Project")
        self.tree.heading("image", text="Image")
        self.tree.heading("checker", text="Color Checker")
        
        self.tree.column("project", width=100)
        self.tree.column("image", width=250)
        self.tree.column("checker", width=250)
        
        scrollbar = ttk.Scrollbar(list_panel, orient=VERTICAL, command=self.tree.yview)
        self.tree.configure(yscroll=scrollbar.set)
        
        self.tree.pack(side=LEFT, fill=BOTH, expand=True)
        scrollbar.pack(side=RIGHT, fill=Y)

        # Bottom Bar for List
        btn_box = ttk.Frame(list_panel, padding=(0, 10, 0, 0))
        btn_box.pack(side=BOTTOM, fill=X)
        ttk.Button(btn_box, text="Clear Queue", command=self._clear_queue, bootstyle="secondary-link").pack(side=RIGHT)
        ttk.Button(btn_box, text="Remove Selected", command=self._remove_selected, bootstyle="warning-link").pack(side=RIGHT, padx=10)

        self._temp_selected_images = []

    def _select_images(self):
        paths = filedialog.askopenfilenames(title="Select Images to Process", filetypes=[("Images", "*.png *.jpg *.jpeg *.bmp *.tiff")])
        if paths:
            self._temp_selected_images = list(paths)
            self.lbl_images.config(text=f"{len(paths)} images selected")

    def _select_checker(self):
        path = filedialog.askopenfilename(title="Select Color Checker", filetypes=[("Images", "*.png *.jpg *.jpeg")])
        if path:
            self.checker_path.set(path)

    def _add_to_queue(self):
        proj = self.cb_project.get()
        if not proj:
            messagebox.showwarning("Missing Info", "Please select a Project.")
            return
        if not self._temp_selected_images:
            messagebox.showwarning("Missing Info", "Please select at least one image.")
            return
        
        checker = self.checker_path.get()
        # Note: checker is optional (None) if not provided, assuming project default might be used or skipped?
        # Task says "pass one colorchecher for each one". I'll assume it's required or strongly recommended for this workflow.
        
        for img_path in self._temp_selected_images:
            item = {
                "project": proj,
                "image": img_path,
                "checker": checker if checker else "Default (Project Config)"
            }
            self.queue.append(item)
            self.tree.insert("", "end", values=(proj, os.path.basename(img_path), os.path.basename(checker) if checker else "Default"))
        
        # Reset selection
        self._temp_selected_images = []
        self.lbl_images.config(text="0 images selected")

    def _remove_selected(self):
        selected = self.tree.selection()
        for item_id in selected:
            # Find index
            idx = self.tree.index(item_id)
            del self.queue[idx]
            self.tree.delete(item_id)

    def _clear_queue(self):
        self.queue = []
        for item in self.tree.get_children():
            self.tree.delete(item)

    def _run_batch(self):
        if not self.queue:
            messagebox.showinfo("Empty Queue", "Add items to the queue first.")
            return

        self.btn_run.config(state=DISABLED, text="Running...")
        self.app.update_idletasks()
        
        success_count = 0
        errors = []

        for i, item in enumerate(self.queue):
            try:
                # Construct Args
                # We reuse the main app's global settings for the common analysis parameters
                # but override project, image, and checker.
                
                bk = int(self.app.blur_kernel_size_var.get())
                blur_kernel = [bk, bk]
                
                args = argparse.Namespace(
                    project=item["project"],
                    image=item["image"],
                    part_number="Batch", # Generic or extract? Pipeline extract
                    thickness="N/A",
                    author=self.app.author_var.get(),
                    department=self.app.department_var.get(),
                    report_title=self.app.report_title_var.get(),
                    debug=self.app.debug_var.get(),
                    
                    # Color Correction
                    color_alignment=self.app.color_alignment_var.get(),
                    color_correction_method=self.app.color_correction_method_var.get(),
                    sample_color_checker=item["checker"] if item["checker"] != "Default (Project Config)" else None,
                    
                    # Alignment
                    alignment=self.app.alignment_var.get(),
                    object_alignment=self.app.object_alignment_var.get(),
                    object_alignment_shadow_removal=self.app.object_alignment_shadow_removal_var.get(),
                    
                    # Masking
                    apply_mask=self.app.apply_mask_var.get(),
                    mask_bg_is_white=self.app.mask_bg_is_white_var.get(),
                    masking_order=self.app.masking_order_var.get(),
                    
                    # Analysis
                    symmetry=self.app.symmetry_var.get(),
                    aggregate=self.app.aggregate_var.get(),
                    agg_kernel_size=int(self.app.agg_kernel_size_var.get()),
                    agg_min_area=float(self.app.agg_min_area_var.get()),
                    agg_density_thresh=float(self.app.agg_density_thresh_var.get()),
                    
                    # Blur
                    blur=self.app.blur_var.get(),
                    blur_kernel=blur_kernel,
                    
                    skip_color_analysis=False,
                    skip_report_generation=True, # CRITICAL: Requested by user
                    load_state_from=None, 
                    save_state_to=None, 
                    video=None, 
                    camera=False
                )
                
                logger.info(f"Batch Processing [{i+1}/{len(self.queue)}]: {os.path.basename(item['image'])}")
                res = run_analysis(args)
                if res:
                    success_count += 1
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Error processing {item['image']}: {e}")
                errors.append(f"{os.path.basename(item['image'])}: {str(e)}")
            
            # Update UI (Primitive progress)
            self.btn_run.config(text=f"Running ({i+1}/{len(self.queue)})...")
            self.app.update_idletasks()

        self.btn_run.config(state=NORMAL, text="RUN BATCH")
        
        msg = f"Batch Complete.\nProcessed: {success_count}/{len(self.queue)}"
        if errors:
            msg += "\n\nErrors:\n" + "\n".join(errors[:5])
            if len(errors) > 5: msg += "\n..."
        
        messagebox.showinfo("Batch Result", msg)

"""
This module provides the `MaskCreator` class for generating and applying masks
from drawing images. It supports creating masks based on transparency and color,
and applying these masks to images to achieve background removal effects.
"""

import cv2
import numpy as np
import os
from pathlib import Path
from src.utils.image_utils import load_image, save_image


class MaskCreator:
    """
    A class to create and apply masks from drawing files.

    It provides methods to generate a binary mask from an input drawing image
    (supporting transparency and white color as background) and to apply this
    mask to another image, typically to make the background transparent.
    """

    def create_mask(
        self,
        drawing_path: str,
        handle_alpha: bool = True,
        treat_white_as_bg: bool = False,
        debug_mode: bool = False,
        output_dir: str = None,
        image_for_debug: np.ndarray = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Creates a binary mask from a drawing image.

        By default, if the image has an alpha channel, non-solid pixels (alpha < 255)
        are treated as background. This can be disabled by setting `handle_alpha` to False.

        Args:
            drawing_path (str): The path to the drawing image file.
            handle_alpha (bool): If True (default), use the alpha channel to create the mask,
                                 treating only fully opaque pixels (alpha=255) as foreground.
                                 If False, generates the mask from grayscale intensity.
            treat_white_as_bg (bool): If True, pure white pixels (255, 255, 255) in the
                                      drawing image are also treated as background and
                                      will be masked out.
            debug_mode (bool): If True, saves intermediate images of the mask creation process.
            output_dir (str): The directory to save debug images to. Required if debug_mode is True.
            image_for_debug (np.ndarray, optional): If provided in debug mode, intermediate masks
                                                will be applied to this image for visualization.

        Returns:
            np.ndarray: A single-channel 8-bit binary mask (foreground is 255, background is 0).
                        This is the correct, standard format for a mask.
                        Returns None if the image cannot be loaded from `drawing_path`.
        """
        drawing_img, alpha_channel = load_image(drawing_path, handle_transparency=True)

        if drawing_img is None:
            return None

        def _save_debug_and_apply(mask_to_save, step_name):
            if not (debug_mode and output_dir):
                return
            base_name = Path(drawing_path).stem
            mask_filename = f"{base_name}_{step_name}_mask.png"
            save_path = os.path.join(output_dir, mask_filename)
            save_image(save_path, mask_to_save)
            print(f"[DEBUG] Saved masking step (raw mask): {save_path}")

            image_to_visualize = (
                image_for_debug if image_for_debug is not None else drawing_img
            )
            if image_to_visualize is not None:
                # The apply_mask function already returns a 4-channel BGRA image
                applied_img = self.apply_mask(image_to_visualize.copy(), mask_to_save)
                applied_filename = (
                    f"{base_name}_{step_name}_applied_to_pipeline_image.png"
                )
                applied_save_path = os.path.join(output_dir, applied_filename)
                save_image(applied_save_path, applied_img)
                print(f"[DEBUG] Saved masked visualization: {applied_save_path}")

        if handle_alpha and alpha_channel is not None:
            # Threshold at 254 to treat only solid pixels (255) as foreground
            _, mask = cv2.threshold(alpha_channel, 254, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY)
            _save_debug_and_apply(mask, "1_from_solid_alpha")
        else:
            gray_img = cv2.cvtColor(drawing_img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
            if debug_mode and output_dir:
                save_image(
                    os.path.join(
                        output_dir, f"{Path(drawing_path).stem}_1a_grayscale_input.png"
                    ),
                    gray_img,
                )
            # Original behavior for non-alpha images
            _, mask = cv2.threshold(gray_img, 1, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY)
            _save_debug_and_apply(mask, "1b_from_grayscale")

        if treat_white_as_bg:
            if len(drawing_img.shape) == 2:
                bgr_img = cv2.cvtColor(drawing_img, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
            else:
                bgr_img = drawing_img

            white_mask = cv2.inRange(bgr_img, (255, 255, 255), (255, 255, 255))
            _save_debug_and_apply(white_mask, "2a_white_pixels")

            inverted_white_mask = cv2.bitwise_not(white_mask)
            mask = cv2.bitwise_and(mask, inverted_white_mask)
            _save_debug_and_apply(mask, "3_final_mask")

        # This function correctly returns the 1-channel binary mask.
        return mask

    def apply_mask(self, image: np.ndarray, mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Applies a binary mask to an image, making the masked-out regions transparent.

        The input image is converted to BGRA format, and its alpha channel is set
        according to the provided `mask`. If the mask dimensions do not match the
        image, the mask is resized using nearest-neighbor interpolation.

        Args:
            image (np.ndarray): The input BGR or grayscale image.
            mask (np.ndarray): The single-channel binary mask (0 for transparent, 255 for opaque).

        Returns:
            np.ndarray: A 4-CHANNEL (BGRA) image with a transparent background
                        where the mask was 0. If `mask` is None, the original
                        image is returned unchanged.
        """
        if mask is None:
            return image

        if len(mask.shape) == 3:
            mask = cv2.cvtColor(mask, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

        if mask.shape[:2] != image.shape[:2]:
            mask = cv2.resize(
                mask,
                (image.shape[1], image.shape[0]),
                interpolation=cv2.INTER_NEAREST,
            )

        # Convert the input image to 4 channels (BGRA) if it isn't already.
        if len(image.shape) == 2:
            image = cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGRA)
        elif image.shape[2] == 3:
            image = cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2BGRA)

        # Set the 4th channel (alpha) using the 1-channel mask.
        image[:, :, 3] = mask

        # This function correctly returns the final 4-channel image.
        return image

def create_and_apply_mask_from_layers(
    image_to_be_processed: np.ndarray,
    drawing_paths: dict, # Changed from project_files
    masking_order: list,
    mask_bg_is_white: bool,
    output_dir: str,
    debug_mode: bool = False,
) -> dict:
    """
    Creates a composite mask from multiple drawing layers and applies it to an image.

    This function encapsulates the logic of iterating through specified drawing layers,
    generating a mask from each, combining them, and applying the final mask to the
    input image. It also handles saving intermediate and final outputs for debugging.

    Args:
        image_to_be_processed (np.ndarray): The input image (BGR or BGRA) to be masked.
        project_files (dict): A dictionary of project file paths.
        masking_order (list): A list of layer numbers (as strings) to combine for the mask.
        mask_bg_is_white (bool): Flag indicating if white should be treated as background.
        output_dir (str): The directory to save output and debug files.
        debug_mode (bool, optional): Enables saving of debug files. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        dict: A dictionary containing:
            - 'image' (np.ndarray | None): The masked image, or None if masking fails.
            - 'debug_paths' (list): A list of dictionaries with title and path for debug reports.
    """
    mask_creator = MaskCreator()
    final_mask = None
    debug_paths = []

    for layer_num in masking_order:
        drawing_path = drawing_paths.get(layer_num)
        if drawing_path:
            if debug_mode:
                print(f"[DEBUG] Attempting to create mask from layer {layer_num} using file: {drawing_path}")
            mask = mask_creator.create_mask(
                str(drawing_path), 
                treat_white_as_bg=mask_bg_is_white, 
                debug_mode=debug_mode, 
                output_dir=output_dir, 
                image_for_debug=image_to_be_processed
            )
            if mask is not None:
                if final_mask is None:
                    final_mask = mask
                else:
                    final_mask = cv2.bitwise_and(final_mask, mask)
                if debug_mode:
                    print(f"[DEBUG] Successfully created and combined mask from layer {layer_num}.")
            elif debug_mode:
                print(f"[WARNING] Failed to create mask from layer {layer_num} file: {drawing_path}")
        elif debug_mode:
            print(f"[WARNING] No path found for technical_drawing_layer_{layer_num} in project configuration.")
    
    if final_mask is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Masking step was enabled but failed to generate a final mask.")

    if debug_mode:
        print(f"[DEBUG] Final mask created. Applying to image.")

    # Use the helper method to apply the mask as a true alpha channel, creating a BGRA image.
    masked_image = mask_creator.apply_mask(image_to_be_processed, final_mask)

    # Calculate statistics
    kept_pixels = np.count_nonzero(final_mask)
    total_pixels = final_mask.shape[0] * final_mask.shape[1]
    kept_percentage = (kept_pixels / total_pixels) * 100 if total_pixels > 0 else 0
    mask_stats = {
        'kept_pixels': kept_pixels,
        'total_pixels': total_pixels,
        'kept_percentage': kept_percentage
    }

    path = os.path.join(output_dir, "masked_image.png")
    save_image(path, masked_image)
    
    if debug_mode:
        mask_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "final_mask.png")
        save_image(mask_path, final_mask)
        debug_paths.append({'title': "Final Applied Mask", 'path': mask_path})
        debug_paths.append({'title': "After Masking", 'path': path})

    return {'image': masked_image, 'debug_paths': debug_paths, 'stats': mask_stats, 'path': path}

messages.content:
I have successfully fixed the persistence issue for drawing mask layers.

### Root Cause:
The issue was due to SQLAlchemy's inability to automatically detect changes within nested JSON structures (like the new modular masking layers) when using standard assignment. As a result, while the layers were being uploaded and added to the in-memory config, they weren't being committed to the database.

### Resolution:
I have integrated **`flag_modified(project, "config")`** across all relevant methods in `ProjectManager` and `ProjectFilePlacerGUI`. This explicitly notifies SQLAlchemy that the JSON configuration has changed, ensuring that:
*   New layers are correctly registered and saved upon upload.
*   Layer labels and "Active" status toggles are persisted.
*   Layer reordering (▲/▼) is correctly stored in the database.
*   Background color settings ("Treat White as BG") are properly saved.

Drawing mask layers will now appear correctly in the GUI after upload and remain persistent across application restarts. I've updated `PROGRESS.md` to reflect these fixes.

async def api_validate_checker(project_id: str):

@api_router.post("/projects/{project_id}/masking/config")
async def api_update_masking_config(project_id: str, config_update: Dict):
    """Updates the modular masking configuration for a project."""
    from src.db import SessionLocal
    from sqlalchemy.orm.attributes import flag_modified
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        project = project_manager.db_manager.get_project(db, name=project_id)
        if not project:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Project not found")
        
        cfg = dict(project.config)
        masking = cfg.setdefault("masking", {})
        
        if "bg_is_white" in config_update:
            masking["bg_is_white"] = config_update["bg_is_white"]
        if "order" in config_update:
            masking["order"] = config_update["order"]
        if "layers" in config_update:
            masking["layers"] = config_update["layers"]
            
        project.config = cfg
        flag_modified(project, "config")
        db.commit()
        project_manager.clear_cache_for_project(project.name)
        return {"success": True}
    finally:
        db.close()

@api_router.delete("/projects/{project_id}/masking/layers/{index}")
async def api_delete_masking_layer(project_id: str, index: int):
    """Deletes a specific masking layer by index."""
    from src.db import SessionLocal, ProjectAsset
    from sqlalchemy.orm.attributes import flag_modified
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        project = project_manager.db_manager.get_project(db, name=project_id)
        if not project:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Project not found")
        
        cfg = dict(project.config)
        masking = cfg.get("masking", {})
        layers = masking.get("layers", [])
        order = masking.get("order", [])
        
        if index < len(layers):
            layer = layers[index]
            # Remove from DB Asset table
            asset = db.query(ProjectAsset).filter_by(project_id=project.id, category="drawing_layer", filename=layer["filename"]).first()
            if asset:
                if os.path.exists(asset.file_path):
                    try: os.remove(asset.file_path)
                    except: pass
                db.delete(asset)
            
            # Update config structures
            layers.pop(index)
            new_order = []
            for o_idx in order:
                if o_idx == index: continue
                new_order.append(o_idx if o_idx < index else o_idx - 1)
            masking["order"] = new_order
            
            project.config = cfg
            flag_modified(project, "config")
            db.commit()
            project_manager.clear_cache_for_project(project.name)
            return {"success": True}
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Invalid layer index")
    finally:
        db.close()

async def api_link_calibration_image(project_id: str, filename: str, parent_asset_id: Annotated[str, Form()]):
    """Links a calibration image to a specific color checker."""
    from src.db import SessionLocal
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        project = project_manager.db_manager.get_project(db, name=project_id)
        if not project:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Project not found")
        
        assets = project_manager.db_manager.list_project_assets(db, project_id=project.id)
        asset = next((a for a in assets if a.category == "calibration_image" and a.filename == filename), None)
        
        if not asset:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Image not found")
            
        p_id = parent_asset_id if parent_asset_id.lower() != "none" else None
        asset.parent_asset_id = p_id
        db.commit()
        project_manager.clear_cache_for_project(project.name)
        return {"success": True}
    finally:
        db.close()

"""
This module provides the `DatasetItemProcessor` class, which is responsible for
extracting and calculating HSV color information from dataset images.

It supports extracting colors from the entire image or from specific points/regions
of interest, and can calculate HSV ranges based on these extracted values.
"""

import cv2
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Tuple, Dict
from pathlib import Path

from src.utils.image_utils import load_image

class DatasetItemProcessor:
    """
    Processes dataset item images to calculate HSV color ranges based on full image
    average or specified points.

    This class provides methods to extract HSV color values from images, either
    from the entire image or from defined regions of interest (ROIs) around points.
    It also includes a method to calculate a basic HSV range from average values.
    """

    def extract_hsv_from_image(
        self, image: np.ndarray, method: str, points: List[Dict] = None, radius: int = 7, blur_kernel_size: int = 0
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Extracts HSV color values from an image based on the specified method.

        Args:
            image (np.ndarray): The input image (already loaded, in BGR format).
            method (str): The extraction method ("full_average" or "points").
            points (List[Dict], optional): A list of point dictionaries for the 'points' method.
            radius (int, optional): Default radius for the 'points' method.
            blur_kernel_size (int, optional): Size of Gaussian Blur kernel (0 for none).

        Returns:
            np.ndarray: An array of HSV color values.
        """
        # Apply non-destructive blur if requested
        if blur_kernel_size > 0:
            k = int(blur_kernel_size)
            if k % 2 == 0: k += 1 # Ensure odd
            if k > 0:
                image = cv2.GaussianBlur(image, (k, k), 0)

        img_bgr, alpha = (image[:, :, :3], image[:, :, 3]) if image.shape[2] == 4 else (image, None)
        hsv_img = cv2.cvtColor(img_bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)

        if method == "full_average":
            pixels = hsv_img[alpha > 0] if alpha is not None else hsv_img.reshape(-1, 3)
            if len(pixels) == 0:
                raise ValueError("No non-transparent pixels found for full image average.")
            return pixels

        elif method == "points":
            if not points:
                raise ValueError("Method 'points' requires a list of points.")
            
            all_pixels = []
            for point in points:
                x, y = point['x'], point['y']
                current_radius = point.get('radius', radius)
                x_min, y_min = max(0, x - current_radius), max(0, y - current_radius)
                x_max, y_max = min(image.shape[1], x + current_radius + 1), min(image.shape[0], y + current_radius + 1)

                roi_hsv = hsv_img[y_min:y_max, x_min:x_max]
                roi_alpha = alpha[y_min:y_max, x_min:x_max] if alpha is not None else None

                pixels = roi_hsv[roi_alpha > 0] if roi_alpha is not None else roi_hsv.reshape(-1, 3)
                if len(pixels) > 0:
                    all_pixels.append(pixels)

            if not all_pixels:
                raise ValueError("No valid pixels found around any specified points.")
            return np.vstack(all_pixels)

        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown extraction method: {method}")

    def calculate_hsv_range(self, hsv_colors: np.ndarray) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Calculates the lower and upper HSV bounds from a list of HSV colors.

        Args:
            hsv_colors (np.ndarray): An array of HSV color values.

        Returns:
            Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]: A tuple containing the lower and upper
                                             HSV bounds.
        """
        if hsv_colors.size == 0:
            return np.array([0, 0, 0]), np.array([179, 255, 255])

        lower_bound = np.min(hsv_colors, axis=0)
        upper_bound = np.max(hsv_colors, axis=0)

        return lower_bound, upper_bound

    def extract_average_hsv_from_image(self, image: np.ndarray, method: str, points: List[Dict] = None, radius: int = 7, blur_kernel_size: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Extracts the average HSV color for each point or for the full image.
        """
        if blur_kernel_size > 0:
            k = int(blur_kernel_size)
            if k % 2 == 0: k += 1 
            if k > 0:
                image = cv2.GaussianBlur(image, (k, k), 0)

        img_bgr, alpha = (image[:, :, :3], image[:, :, 3]) if image.shape[2] == 4 else (image, None)
        hsv_img = cv2.cvtColor(img_bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)

        if method == "full_average":
            pixels = hsv_img[alpha > 0] if alpha is not None else hsv_img.reshape(-1, 3)
            if len(pixels) == 0:
                return np.array([])
            avg_color = np.mean(pixels, axis=0)
            return np.array([avg_color])

        elif method == "points":
            if not points:
                raise ValueError("Method 'points' requires a list of points.")
            
            average_colors = []
            for point in points:
                x, y = point['x'], point['y']
                current_radius = point.get('radius', radius)
                x_min, y_min = max(0, x - current_radius), max(0, y - current_radius)
                x_max, y_max = min(image.shape[1], x + current_radius + 1), min(image.shape[0], y + current_radius + 1)

                roi_hsv = hsv_img[y_min:y_max, x_min:x_max]
                roi_alpha = alpha[y_min:y_max, x_min:x_max] if alpha is not None else None

                pixels = roi_hsv[roi_alpha > 0] if roi_alpha is not None else roi_hsv.reshape(-1, 3)
                if len(pixels) > 0:
                    avg_color = np.mean(pixels, axis=0)
                    average_colors.append(avg_color)

            if not average_colors:
                return np.array([])
            return np.array(average_colors)

        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown extraction method: {method}")

import tkinter as tk

        ).pack(fill=X, pady=5)

        ttk.Separator(side_panel, orient=HORIZONTAL).pack(fill=X, pady=10)

        # Zone 1: Zoom

        m_frame = ttk.Labelframe(console, text="Mode", padding=5)

        # Zone 3: Parameters (Cluster) - Moved to Left of Blur
        self.p_frame = ttk.Labelframe(console, text="Parameters", padding=5)

        # Row 1: Cluster Option
        f_cluster = ttk.Frame(self.p_frame)
        f_cluster.pack(fill=X, pady=2)
        
        self.rb_cluster = ttk.Radiobutton(
            f_cluster, 
            text="K-Means:", 
            variable=self.area_method, 
            value="cluster", 
            command=self._on_method_change
        )
        self.rb_cluster.pack(side=LEFT)
        
        self.cluster_entry = ttk.Entry(f_cluster, textvariable=self.num_clusters_var, width=4)
        self.cluster_entry.pack(side=LEFT, padx=5)

        # Row 2: Unique Colors Option
        self.rb_colors = ttk.Radiobutton(
            self.p_frame, 
            text="Unique Colors", 
            variable=self.area_method, 
            value="colors", 
            command=self._on_method_change
        )
        self.rb_colors.pack(fill=X, pady=2, anchor=W)

        # Zone 4: Blur Tool
        b_frame = ttk.Labelframe(console, text="Blur", padding=5)
        b_frame.pack(side=LEFT, padx=(0, 10), fill=Y)

        # Container for vertical stack
        b_inner = ttk.Frame(b_frame)
        b_inner.pack(expand=True, fill=BOTH)

        ttk.Scale(
            b_inner,
            from_=0,
            to=20,
            variable=self.blur_var,
            command=self._on_blur_change,
            length=100,
        ).pack(side=TOP, padx=5)
        self.blur_status_label = ttk.Label(
            b_inner, text="0 (0%)", font=("Helvetica", 8)
        )
        self.blur_status_label.pack(side=TOP)

        self._update_bindings()

    def _on_method_change(self):
        """When user clicks a parameter radio, switch to Area mode automatically."""
        self.mode.set("area")
        self._update_bindings()

    def _update_bindings(self):
        self.canvas.unbind("<Button-1>")
        self.canvas.unbind("<ButtonPress-1>")
        self.canvas.unbind("<B1-Motion>")
        self.canvas.unbind("<ButtonRelease-1>")

        mode = self.mode.get()
        method = self.area_method.get()
        
        # --- UI State Management ---
        if mode in ["points", "delete"]:
            # Disable Parameters controls
            self.cluster_entry.configure(state="disabled")
            self.rb_cluster.configure(state="disabled")
            self.rb_colors.configure(state="disabled")
        else:
            # Enable Parameters controls
            self.rb_cluster.configure(state="normal")
            self.rb_colors.configure(state="normal")
            
            # If K-Means (cluster) is selected, enable entry
            if method == "cluster":
                self.cluster_entry.configure(state="normal")
            else:
                self.cluster_entry.configure(state="disabled")

        if mode == "points":
            self.canvas.config(cursor="cross")
            self.canvas.bind("<Button-1>", self._handle_point_click)
        elif mode == "area":
            self.canvas.config(cursor="tcross")
            self.canvas.bind("<ButtonPress-1>", self._on_area_press)
            self.canvas.bind("<B1-Motion>", self._on_area_drag)
            self.canvas.bind("<ButtonRelease-1>", self._on_area_release)
        elif mode == "delete":
            self.canvas.config(cursor="X_cursor")
            self.canvas.bind("<Button-1>", self._handle_delete_click)

        # Always enable Pan/Zoom
        self.canvas.bind("<Control-MouseWheel>", self._on_mouse_wheel)
        self.canvas.bind("<ButtonPress-2>", self._on_drag_start)  # Middle click pan
        self.canvas.bind("<B2-Motion>", self._on_drag_motion)

    # --- Loading & Drawing Logic ---
    def load_config(self):
        try:
            config_data = self.project_manager._get_dataset_item_processing_config(
                self.project_name
            )
            for img_config in config_data.image_configs:
                if img_config.method == "points" and img_config.points:
                    self.image_points[img_config.filename] = [
                        p.model_dump() for p in img_config.points
                    ]
        except Exception:
            pass

    def load_image(self):
        image_path = self.image_paths[self.current_image_index]
        fname = os.path.basename(image_path)
        self.image_label.config(
            text=f"Image {self.current_image_index + 1} / {len(self.image_paths)}: {fname}"
        )

        self.current_cv_image = cv2.imread(str(image_path))
        if self.current_cv_image is None:
            return

        # Load Blur Setting from Config specifically for this image
        try:
            config_data = self.project_manager._get_dataset_item_processing_config(
                self.project_name
            )
            img_cfg = next(
                (c for c in config_data.image_configs if c.filename == fname), None
            )
            if img_cfg:
                self.blur_var.set(img_cfg.blur_kernel_size)
            else:
                self.blur_var.set(0)
        except:
            self.blur_var.set(0)

        # Apply Blur (Visualization)
        k = int(float(self.blur_var.get()))
        if k % 2 == 0:
            k += 1
        if k > 1:
            self.blurred_cv_image = cv2.GaussianBlur(self.current_cv_image, (k, k), 0)
        else:
            self.blurred_cv_image = self.current_cv_image.copy()

        # Fit to View (Approx)
        win_w, win_h = 1000, 700
        h, w, _ = self.current_cv_image.shape
        self.zoom_level = min(win_w / w, win_h / h, 1.0) * 0.9

        self.redraw_canvas()
        self._update_point_list()

        # Update label
        val = self.blur_var.get()
        pct = int((val / 20) * 100)
        if hasattr(self, "blur_status_label"):
            self.blur_status_label.config(text=f"{int(val)} ({pct}%)")

    def _on_blur_change(self, val):
        if self.current_cv_image is None:
            return
        k = int(float(val))

        # Update label first
        pct = int((float(val) / 20) * 100)
        if hasattr(self, "blur_status_label"):
            self.blur_status_label.config(text=f"{k} ({pct}%)")

        if k % 2 == 0:
            k += 1  # Kernel size must be odd
        if k < 1:
            k = 1

        if k == 1:
            self.blurred_cv_image = self.current_cv_image.copy()
        else:
            self.blurred_cv_image = cv2.GaussianBlur(self.current_cv_image, (k, k), 0)

        self.redraw_canvas()
        self._update_point_list()  # Colors might change if sampling from blurred image

    def redraw_canvas(self):
        if self.blurred_cv_image is None:
            return
        self.canvas.delete("all")

        h, w, _ = self.blurred_cv_image.shape
        nw, nh = int(w * self.zoom_level), int(h * self.zoom_level)

        img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(self.blurred_cv_image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
        pil_img = Image.fromarray(img_rgb).resize((nw, nh), Image.Resampling.BILINEAR)
        self.current_photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(image=pil_img)

        # Center the image
        c_w = self.canvas.winfo_width()
        c_h = self.canvas.winfo_height()

        colors = self.app.get_current_colors() if self.app else {}
        bg_col = colors.get("canvas_bg", "#1e1e1e")
        self.canvas.config(bg=bg_col)

        x_offset = max(0, (c_w - nw) // 2)
        y_offset = max(0, (c_h - nh) // 2)

        self.canvas.config(scrollregion=(0, 0, max(nw, c_w), max(nh, c_h)))
        self.canvas.create_image(
            x_offset, y_offset, anchor=tk.NW, image=self.current_photo
        )

        self.draw_points(x_offset, y_offset)
        self.canvas_offset_x = x_offset
        self.canvas_offset_y = y_offset

    def draw_points(self, off_x, off_y):
        self.canvas.delete("point")
        self.canvas.delete("selection_ring")

        fname = os.path.basename(self.image_paths[self.current_image_index])
        points = self.image_points.get(fname, [])

        colors = self.app.get_current_colors() if self.app else {}
        default_col = colors.get("canvas_point", "#00ff00")

        img_h, img_w = 0, 0
        if self.blurred_cv_image is not None:
            img_h, img_w = self.blurred_cv_image.shape[:2]

        for i, p in enumerate(points):
            cx = (p["x"] * self.zoom_level) + off_x
            cy = (p["y"] * self.zoom_level) + off_y
            r = p.get("radius", 7)

            fill_col = default_col
            if self.blurred_cv_image is not None:
                ix, iy = int(p["x"]), int(p["y"])
                if 0 <= ix < img_w and 0 <= iy < img_h:
                    b, g, r_val = self.blurred_cv_image[iy, ix]
                    fill_col = f"#{int(r_val):02x}{int(g):02x}{int(b):02x}"

            self.canvas.create_oval(
                cx - r,
                cy - r,
                cx + r,
                cy + r,
                fill=fill_col,
                outline="black",
                width=2,
                tags=("point", f"p_{i}"),
            )

            # Highlight selected
            if i in self.selected_point_indices:
                self.canvas.create_oval(
                    cx - r - 3,
                    cy - r - 3,
                    cx + r + 3,
                    cy + r + 3,
                    outline="white",
                    width=2,
                    tags="selection_ring",
                )

    def _update_point_list(self):
        # Clear
        for item in self.tree.get_children():
            self.tree.delete(item)

        fname = os.path.basename(self.image_paths[self.current_image_index])
        points = self.image_points.get(fname, [])

        img_h, img_w = 0, 0
        if self.blurred_cv_image is not None:
            img_h, img_w = self.blurred_cv_image.shape[:2]

        for i, p in enumerate(points):
            rgb_text = "N/A"
            hex_col = "#333333"  # Default
            fg_col = "white"

            if self.blurred_cv_image is not None:
                ix, iy = int(p["x"]), int(p["y"])
                if 0 <= ix < img_w and 0 <= iy < img_h:
                    b, g, r = self.blurred_cv_image[iy, ix]
                    rgb_text = f"({r}, {g}, {b})"
                    hex_col = f"#{int(r):02x}{int(g):02x}{int(b):02x}"

                    # Simple brightness for text contrast
                    brightness = (int(r) * 299 + int(g) * 587 + int(b) * 114) / 1000
                    fg_col = "black" if brightness > 128 else "white"

            tag_name = f"row_{i}"
            self.tree.insert(
                "", "end", iid=str(i), values=(rgb_text,), tags=(tag_name,)
            )
            self.tree.tag_configure(tag_name, background=hex_col, foreground=fg_col)

    def _on_tree_select(self, event):
        selected_items = self.tree.selection()
        self.selected_point_indices = [int(item) for item in selected_items]
        self.redraw_canvas()

    def _delete_selected_points(self):
        fname = os.path.basename(self.image_paths[self.current_image_index])
        points = self.image_points.get(fname, [])
        if not points:
            return

        # Sort indices in descending order to avoid index shifting issues
        indices_to_delete = sorted(self.selected_point_indices, reverse=True)

        for idx in indices_to_delete:
            if 0 <= idx < len(points):
                points.pop(idx)

        self.selected_point_indices = []
        self._update_point_list()
        self.redraw_canvas()

    def _zoom(self, factor):
        self.zoom_level *= factor
        self.redraw_canvas()

    def _on_mouse_wheel(self, event):
        factor = 1.1 if (event.delta > 0 or event.num == 4) else 0.9
        self._zoom(factor)
        return "break"

    def _on_drag_start(self, event):
        self.canvas.scan_mark(event.x, event.y)

    def _on_drag_motion(self, event):
        self.canvas.scan_dragto(event.x, event.y, gain=1)

    # --- Interaction Logic ---
    def _to_img_coords(self, cx, cy):
        # Inverse of draw_points logic
        # cx = (img_x * zoom) + offset  => img_x = (cx - offset) / zoom
        ix = int(
            (self.canvas.canvasx(cx) - getattr(self, "canvas_offset_x", 0))
            / self.zoom_level
        )
        iy = int(
            (self.canvas.canvasy(cy) - getattr(self, "canvas_offset_y", 0))
            / self.zoom_level
        )
        return ix, iy

    def _handle_point_click(self, event):
        ix, iy = self._to_img_coords(event.x, event.y)
        fname = os.path.basename(self.image_paths[self.current_image_index])
        if fname not in self.image_points:
            self.image_points[fname] = []
        self.image_points[fname].append({"x": ix, "y": iy, "radius": 7})
        self.redraw_canvas()
        self._update_point_list()

    def _handle_delete_click(self, event):
        ix, iy = self._to_img_coords(event.x, event.y)
        fname = os.path.basename(self.image_paths[self.current_image_index])
        points = self.image_points.get(fname, [])
        if not points:
            return

        # Simple distance check
        for i, p in enumerate(points):
            dist = np.sqrt((p["x"] - ix) ** 2 + (p["y"] - iy) ** 2)
            if dist <= (p.get("radius", 7) / self.zoom_level) + 5:  # Tolerance
                points.pop(i)
                self.redraw_canvas()
                self._update_point_list()
                break

    # --- Area Logic (Brief) ---
    def _on_area_press(self, e):
        self.start_x = self.canvas.canvasx(e.x)
        self.start_y = self.canvas.canvasy(e.y)
        if self.rect:
            self.canvas.delete(self.rect)
        self.rect = self.canvas.create_rectangle(
            self.start_x,
            self.start_y,
            self.start_x,
            self.start_y,
            outline="cyan",
            dash=(4, 2),
        )

    def _on_area_drag(self, e):
        cur_x, cur_y = self.canvas.canvasx(e.x), self.canvas.canvasy(e.y)
        self.canvas.coords(self.rect, self.start_x, self.start_y, cur_x, cur_y)

    def _on_area_release(self, e):
        if not self.rect:
            return
        
        # Calculate Canvas Coordinates of the rectangle
        # Note: self.start_x/y are already canvas coords (set in _on_area_press)
        cur_x = self.canvas.canvasx(e.x)
        cur_y = self.canvas.canvasy(e.y)
        
        cx1, cy1 = min(self.start_x, cur_x), min(self.start_y, cur_y)
        cx2, cy2 = max(self.start_x, cur_x), max(self.start_y, cur_y)
        
        self.canvas.delete(self.rect)
        self.rect = None
        
        if self.current_cv_image is None: return
        
        # Convert to Image Coordinates directly
        # img_x = (canvas_x - offset) / zoom
        off_x = getattr(self, "canvas_offset_x", 0)
        off_y = getattr(self, "canvas_offset_y", 0)
        
        rx1 = int((cx1 - off_x) / self.zoom_level)
        ry1 = int((cy1 - off_y) / self.zoom_level)
        rx2 = int((cx2 - off_x) / self.zoom_level)
        ry2 = int((cy2 - off_y) / self.zoom_level)
        
        h, w = self.current_cv_image.shape[:2]
        
        # Clamp to image bounds
        x1 = int(max(0, min(rx1, w)))
        y1 = int(max(0, min(ry1, h)))
        x2 = int(max(0, min(rx2, w)))
        y2 = int(max(0, min(ry2, h)))

        if abs(x2 - x1) > 2 and abs(y2 - y1) > 2:
            if self.area_method.get() == "cluster":
                self._perform_clustering(x1, y1, x2, y2)
            elif self.area_method.get() == "colors":
                self._perform_getcolors(x1, y1, x2, y2)

    def _perform_clustering(self, x1, y1, x2, y2):
        try:
            k = int(self.num_clusters_var.get())
        except:
            return
            
        roi = self.blurred_cv_image[y1:y2, x1:x2]
        if roi.size == 0: return
        
        pixels = roi.reshape(-1, 3).astype(np.float32)
        n_pixels = pixels.shape[0]
        
        if n_pixels == 0: return
        if k > n_pixels: k = n_pixels
        if k < 1: return

        _, _, centers = cv2.kmeans(
            pixels,
            k,
            None,
            (cv2.TERM_CRITERIA_EPS + cv2.TERM_CRITERIA_MAX_ITER, 10, 1.0),
            10,
            cv2.KMEANS_RANDOM_CENTERS,
        )

        new_pts = []
        for c in centers:
            dists = np.linalg.norm(pixels - c, axis=1)
            idx = np.argmin(dists)
            ry, rx = np.unravel_index(idx, (roi.shape[0], roi.shape[1]))
            new_pts.append({"x": int(rx + x1), "y": int(ry + y1), "radius": 7})

        fname = os.path.basename(self.image_paths[self.current_image_index])
        if fname not in self.image_points:
            self.image_points[fname] = []
        self.image_points[fname].extend(new_pts)
        self.redraw_canvas()
        self._update_point_list()

    def _perform_getcolors(self, x1, y1, x2, y2):
        roi = self.blurred_cv_image[y1:y2, x1:x2]
        if roi.size == 0: return
        
        # Use NumPy for robust and fast unique color extraction
        # This avoids the PIL maxcolors limit and slow python loops
        pixels = roi.reshape(-1, 3)
        _, indices = np.unique(pixels, axis=0, return_index=True)
        
        # Limit the number of points to avoid UI freezing if user selects a massive area
        # 10,000 points is a reasonable safety cap for a manual UI tool
        MAX_UI_POINTS = 10000
        if len(indices) > MAX_UI_POINTS:
            # If too many, subsample or just warn? Subsampling is safer.
            indices = np.random.choice(indices, MAX_UI_POINTS, replace=False)
        
        new_pts = []
        h, w = roi.shape[:2]
        
        for idx in indices:
            ry, rx = np.unravel_index(idx, (h, w))
            new_pts.append({"x": int(rx + x1), "y": int(ry + y1), "radius": 7})

        fname = os.path.basename(self.image_paths[self.current_image_index])
        if fname not in self.image_points:
            self.image_points[fname] = []
        self.image_points[fname].extend(new_pts)
        self.redraw_canvas()
        self._update_point_list()

    def next_image(self):
        if self.current_image_index < len(self.image_paths) - 1:
            self.current_image_index += 1
            self.load_image()

    def prev_image(self):
        if self.current_image_index > 0:
            self.current_image_index -= 1
            self.load_image()

    def clear_points(self):
        fname = os.path.basename(self.image_paths[self.current_image_index])
        self.image_points[fname] = []
        self.redraw_canvas()
        self._update_point_list()

    def save_and_close(self):
        try:
            for path in self.image_paths:
                fname = os.path.basename(path)
                pts = self.image_points.get(fname)
                if pts is not None:
                    # Pass the current blur setting
                    blur_k = int(float(self.blur_var.get()))
                    if blur_k % 2 == 0 and blur_k > 0:
                        blur_k += 1

                    self.project_manager.update_dataset_item_points(
                        self.project_name, fname, pts, blur_kernel_size=blur_k
                    )

            self.destroy()
            messagebox.showinfo("Saved", "Configuration saved.")
        except Exception as e:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", str(e))

import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import messagebox
import ttkbootstrap as ttk
from ttkbootstrap.constants import *
import numpy as np
import webbrowser
import os
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import plotly.graph_objects as go
    HAS_PLOTLY = True
except ImportError:
    HAS_PLOTLY = False

from src.project_management.manager import ProjectManager
from src.utils.logging_utils import setup_logger

logger = setup_logger(__name__)

class ProfileVisualizerGUI(ttk.Frame):
    def __init__(self, master, project_name):
        super().__init__(master)
        self.project_name = project_name
        self.project_manager = ProjectManager()
        self.data = None
        
        self._build_ui()
        self.load_data()

    def _build_ui(self):
        self.pack(fill=BOTH, expand=True)
        
        # Header
        hdr = ttk.Frame(self, padding=10, bootstyle="info")
        hdr.pack(fill=X)
        ttk.Label(hdr, text=f"Multivariate Color Profile: {self.project_name}", font=("Helvetica", 14, "bold"), bootstyle="inverse-info").pack(side=LEFT)

        # Content
        content = ttk.Frame(self, padding=20)
        content.pack(fill=BOTH, expand=True)
        
        # Statistics Panel
        self.stats_frame = ttk.Labelframe(content, text="Profile Statistics", padding=15)
        self.stats_frame.pack(fill=X, pady=(0, 20))
        
        self.lbl_samples = ttk.Label(self.stats_frame, text="Samples: Loading...")
        self.lbl_samples.pack(anchor="w")
        self.lbl_outliers = ttk.Label(self.stats_frame, text="Outliers: Loading...")
        self.lbl_outliers.pack(anchor="w")
        self.lbl_threshold = ttk.Label(self.stats_frame, text="Mahalanobis Threshold: Loading...")
        self.lbl_threshold.pack(anchor="w")

        # Plot Action
        btn_frame = ttk.Frame(content)
        btn_frame.pack(fill=X)
        
        if HAS_PLOTLY:
            self.btn_plot = ttk.Button(btn_frame, text="Open Interactive Plotly Chart ↗", command=self.generate_plotly_chart, bootstyle="success", width=30)
            self.btn_plot.pack(ipady=10)
            ttk.Label(btn_frame, text="(Opens in default web browser)", font=("Helvetica", 8), foreground="gray").pack(pady=5)
        else:
            ttk.Label(btn_frame, text="Plotly not installed. Please run: pip install plotly", bootstyle="danger").pack()

    def load_data(self):
        try:
            # Force debug mode to ensure we get dataset_debug_info
            self.data = self.project_manager.get_project_data(self.project_name, debug_mode=True)
            self._update_stats()
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to load project data: {e}")
            messagebox.showerror("Error", f"Failed to load data: {e}")

    def _update_stats(self):
        if not self.data: return
        
        profile = self.data.get("multivariate_color_profile", {})
        debug_info = self.data.get("dataset_debug_info", [])
        
        total_points = 0
        total_outliers = 0
        
        for item in debug_info:
            hsv = item.get("hsv_colors", [])
            outliers = item.get("outlier_mask", [])
            total_points += len(hsv)
            total_outliers += sum(outliers)
            
        self.lbl_samples.config(text=f"Total Calibration Points: {total_points}")
        self.lbl_outliers.config(text=f"Detected Outliers: {total_outliers} ({total_outliers/total_points*100:.2f}% if points > 0 else 0)")
        self.lbl_threshold.config(text=f"Method: One-Class SVM (Nu={profile.get('svm_params', {}).get('nu', 0.05)})")

    def generate_plotly_chart(self):
        if not self.data or not HAS_PLOTLY: return
        
        try:
            profile = self.data.get("multivariate_color_profile", {})
            debug_info = self.data.get("dataset_debug_info", [])
            
            # 1. Collect Points
            # Subsample for performance
            MAX_POINTS = 50000
            
            all_hsv = []
            all_bgr = []
            all_status = []
            
            for item in debug_info:
                hsvs = item.get("hsv_colors", [])
                bgrs = item.get("bgr_colors", [])
                masks = item.get("outlier_mask", [])
                
                if hsvs:
                    all_hsv.extend(hsvs)
                    all_bgr.extend(bgrs)
                    all_status.extend(masks)
            
            if not all_hsv:
                messagebox.showinfo("Info", "No calibration points found.")
                return

            # Downsample
            if len(all_hsv) > MAX_POINTS:
                indices = np.random.choice(len(all_hsv), MAX_POINTS, replace=False)
                all_hsv = np.array(all_hsv)[indices]
                all_bgr = np.array(all_bgr)[indices]
                all_status = np.array(all_status)[indices]
            else:
                all_hsv = np.array(all_hsv)
                all_bgr = np.array(all_bgr)
                all_status = np.array(all_status)

            # Split Inliers/Outliers
            mask = all_status.astype(bool)
            
            # Helper: HSV to Cartesian
            # X = S * cos(H), Y = S * sin(H), Z = V
            def to_cartesian(h, s, v):
                h_rad = h * (2 * np.pi / 180.0)
                x = s * np.cos(h_rad)
                y = s * np.sin(h_rad)
                z = v
                return x, y, z

            # Colors for Plotly
            def bgr_to_css(bgr_arr):
                return [f'rgb({c[2]},{c[1]},{c[0]})' for c in bgr_arr]

            fig = go.Figure()

            # Plot Inliers (Cartesian)
            if len(all_hsv[~mask]) > 0:
                ix, iy, iz = to_cartesian(all_hsv[~mask][:, 0], all_hsv[~mask][:, 1], all_hsv[~mask][:, 2])
                fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d(
                    x=ix, y=iy, z=iz,
                    mode='markers',
                    marker=dict(size=3, color=bgr_to_css(all_bgr[~mask]), opacity=0.6),
                    name='Inliers (Support)'
                ))

            # Plot Outliers (Cartesian)
            if len(all_hsv[mask]) > 0:
                ox, oy, oz = to_cartesian(all_hsv[mask][:, 0], all_hsv[mask][:, 1], all_hsv[mask][:, 2])
                fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d(
                    x=ox, y=oy, z=oz,
                    mode='markers',
                    marker=dict(
                        size=3, 
                        color=bgr_to_css(all_bgr[mask]), 
                        opacity=0.8
                    ),
                    name='Outliers'
                ))

            # Plot SVM Mesh (Already Cartesian definition)
            if 'mesh' in profile:
                mesh_data = profile['mesh']
                if mesh_data.get('vertices') and mesh_data.get('faces'):
                    verts = np.array(mesh_data['vertices'])
                    faces = np.array(mesh_data['faces'])
                    
                    fig.add_trace(go.Mesh3d(
                        x=verts[:, 0], 
                        y=verts[:, 1], 
                        z=verts[:, 2],
                        i=faces[:, 0], 
                        j=faces[:, 1], 
                        k=faces[:, 2],
                        color='cyan',
                        opacity=0.2,
                        name='SVM Boundary'
                    ))

            fig.update_layout(
                title=f"One-Class SVM Color Profile: {self.project_name}",
                scene=dict(
                    xaxis_title='X (S * cos H)',
                    yaxis_title='Y (S * sin H)',
                    zaxis_title='Z (Value)',
                    # Aspect ratio preserving for true shape
                    aspectmode='data'
                ),
                margin=dict(l=0, r=0, b=0, t=40)
            )
            
            fig.show()

        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Plotting error: {e}")
            messagebox.showerror("Error", f"Could not generate plot: {e}")
